scales.name: Dorian
scales.note: minor with a bright 6th — 'So What' (Miles Davis), 'Scarborough Fair'

scales.name: Phrygian
scales.note: dark, Spanish — flamenco and metal riffs live here

scales.name: Lydian
scales.note: major with a raised 4th, floaty — The Simpsons theme

scales.name: Mixolydian
scales.note: major with a flat 7th — 'Sweet Home Alabama', 'Norwegian Wood'

scales.name: Harmonic minor
scales.note: raised 7th gives an exotic pull — 'Hava Nagila'

scales.name: Melodic minor
scales.note: jazz minor — the sound over m(maj7) chords

scales.name: Major pentatonic
scales.note: five notes, no wrong ones — 'My Girl' riff (Temptations)

scales.name: Minor pentatonic
scales.note: the rock-solo scale — nearly every blues lick starts here

scales.name: Blues
scales.note: minor pentatonic + flat 5 — 'Sunshine of Your Love' (Cream)

scales.name: Whole tone
scales.note: dream-sequence blur — 'You Are the Sunshine of My Life' intro

scales.name: Locrian
scales.note: half-diminished tonic — theory candy, almost never home

chords.name: major seventh
chords.note: 'The Girl from Ipanema' — the opening Fmaj7

chords.name: minor seventh
chords.note: every ii chord in a ii–V–I; 'So What' voicings

chords.name: dominant seventh
chords.note: 'Johnny B. Goode' — the engine of the blues

chords.name: diminished seventh
chords.note: the villain sting; passing chord in 'Michelle' (Beatles)

chords.name: suspended 2nd
chords.note: open and ambiguous — pop intros before the resolve

chords.name: major sixth
chords.note: the final chord of 'She Loves You' (Beatles)

chords.name: minor-major seventh
chords.note: the James Bond theme's final chord
